videos.t: Nail Varnish Tutorial - Binary numbers
videos.desc:
Here's Katie's introduction to how to make your nails display a mathematical secret message, using glitter! Use binary numbers, like computers do, to express yourself in glittery ones and non-glittery zeroes.

Binary Nail Cheat Sheet is here: bit.ly/binarycheatsheet

If you're interested, here's a related puzzle I've posted over at The Aperiodical: http://aperiodical.com/2016/05/katies-binary-nails-tutorial-and-a-puzzle/

Music by Kevin Macleod/incompetech.com

videos.desc:
Thanks to Marjut Salminen from fbsoc.fi for her kind permission to tell this story and reproduce the trick here! For more information about MathsJam: mathsjam.com

Also: YouTube appears to have cut off the last 10 seconds of my video! Here's what happened next: https://youtu.be/JHQB1R6pPUc

videos.t: Cutting an oval pizza into equal area slices
videos.desc:
Struggling to cut your elliptical pizza up into equal pieces? Here's a nice method for doing that, and a bit of an idea why it works.

Thanks to Kevin Macleod/incompetech.com as usual for blippy tunes.

videos.t: How to draw an egg!
videos.desc: Using only a pair of compasses, ruler and pencil, here's how to construct an egg shape from arcs of circles. Blippy music, as always, by Kevin Macleod at incompetech.com. Grammar pedantry by Bill Steckles.

videos.t: A couple of mathematical games
videos.desc:
Katie shows one of her mathematical friends some new games she's found recently.

Also: to clarify, when I say 'hundreds' I of course mean 84. And if you notice something weird going on in the close-up shots, bear in mind that I'm ambidextrous.

I'm also hoping to shortly do a giveaway of the cards used in the video - follow me on Twitter (@stecks) for details of how I can post some lucky winners a set of cards in the actual post.

Special guest star: Dr James Grime youtube.com/singingbanana
James' video on the Game of Nine: https://youtu.be/ue4Baa8Mhn8

videos.t: Pi km run around a 10m circle
videos.desc:
For Sport Relief 2018, I'm running πkm every day in March. Today I've done it by running around the circumference of a 10m diameter circle 100 times, giving a total distance run of πkm. Sponsor me to keep running at pikm.run.

Sport Relief: sportrelief.com

videos.t: Katie's #MegaFavNumbers - the MEGISTON, and Steinhaus-Moser notation
videos.desc:
This video is part of the MegaFavNumbers project. Maths YouTubers have come together to make videos about their favourite numbers bigger than one million, which we are calling #MegafavNumbers.

We want *you*, the viewers, to join in! Make your own video about your favourite mega-number. You can think of a cool big number, or think of a cool topic first and hang a mega-number on it.

Upload your videos to YouTube with the hashtag #MegaFavNumbers and with MegaFavNumbers in the title, and your video will be added to the megafavnumbers playlist.

Submit your videos anytime before Wednesday 2nd Sep

videos.t: Fold and one cut snowflake!
videos.desc:
Music: the first blip blop noel by dma-sc, CC BY-NC-ND 3.0

Since I've talked about the Fold and Cut theorem before, and have also previously been annoyed about people making non-hexagonal snowflakes, I sometimes get asked if it's possible to cut out a real hexagonal snowflake with one straight cut. Here's the answer!

Fold and Cut Theorem, on Numberphile
https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=ZREp1mAPKTM
Snowflake or Snow-fake, on Think Maths
https://think-maths.co.uk/snowflake-or-snow-fake
#snowfake hashtag on Twitter, to which I contribute most years:
https://twitter.com/search?q=%23snowfake

videos.t: Maths in the Spiderman: No Way Home Credits
videos.desc:
Join me and fellow maths/Marvel fan Jimi for a walk through the end credits of Spiderman: No Way Home, and a chat about some of the interesting mathematical things we spot therein.

More info about the pointy shapes we mention around 6:45 can be found here: https://aperiodical.com/2018/07/the-big-internet-math-off-round-1-peter-rowlett-v-alison-kiddle/

Visit the Aperiodical: https://aperiodical.com

videos.desc:

videos.t: Animation Generation Collaboration entry for April 2025: Katie Steckles
videos.desc:
This video is my entry for the April edition of the TMiP @talkingmathsinpublic Animation Generation Collaboration (details at https://talkingmathsinpublic.uk/animation ), where we all build the same animation illustrating a maths concept in our own different hacky and inventive ways, and share our process videos.

I'm using MacOS Keynote, as I do for all my slides and animations, and as you'll see I've done a slightly wrong but perfectly adequate job of creating an animation to show a net of a polyhedron folding up into a polyhedron.

Thanks to whoever made https://www.omnicalculator.com/math/

videos.t: Animation Generation Collaboration entry for May 2025: Katie Steckles
videos.desc:
This video is my entry for the May edition of the TMiP @talkingmathsinpublic  Animation Generation Collaboration (details at https://talkingmathsinpublic.uk/animation ), where we all build the same animation illustrating a maths concept in our own different hacky and inventive ways, and share our process videos.

I'm using MacOS Keynote, as I do for all my slides and animations, and as you'll see I've done an animation that proves Pythagoras' theorem (just about, maybe a couple of pixels out here and there) with labels that move with the pieces.

videos.t: Why Can't People Draw Pictures of Real Noughts and Crosses Games?
videos.desc:
Join Katie and her combinatorial game theory pal Peter Rowlett for a look at some of the pictures people have drawn of tic-tac-toe games, and why some of them are real bad.

See also:
Tic-Tac-Toe (with Xs only) - Numberphile https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=ktPvjr1tiKk
https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Notakto

Update: moaning on YouTube is super effective! They've fixed the image at https://commons.m.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:Tic-Tac-Toe-Possible_Grid.png

videos.t: Animation Generation Collaboration entry for June 2025: Katie Steckles
videos.desc:
This video is my (slightly belated) entry for the June edition of the TMiP @talkingmathsinpublic  Animation Generation Collaboration (details at https://talkingmathsinpublic.uk/animation ), where we all build the same animation illustrating a maths concept in our own different hacky and inventive ways, and share our process videos.

I'm using MacOS Keynote, as I do for all my slides and animations, and as you'll see I've done an animation that shows a pursuit curve.

videos.t: How good is my card shuffling machine?
videos.desc:
Katie's obtained a new gadget, which is a playing card shuffling machine - and she's invited Professor Kevin Houston, maths/cards guy, to have a chat about maths and shuffling.

Diaconis/Bayer paper: https://www.stat.berkeley.edu/~aldous/157/Papers/bayer_diaconis.pdf
More recent work on non-halved decks: https://www.quantamagazine.org/seven-perfect-shuffles-randomize-a-deck-of-cards-but-how-many-sloppy-ones-20260617/ (yes, the title of that article uses the word 'perfect' to mean a half-and-half split, not a perfect shuffle)
Alex Elmsley, on Wikipedia: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alex_Elmsle
